summary: Iteration 12 — Email+Password auth, landing polish (2-link nav, orbs, logos, CTAs), /auth page, and Executive KPI unification all verified. Backend 73/74 pass (56 prior + 11 bulk + 7 new pwd-auth passing). One backend bug: brute-force lockout relies on request.client.host which resolves to different K8s pod IPs per request, so the 5-fail 429 never triggers in production-like proxied environments. Frontend: landing nav = exactly ['Platform','ROI'] + 'Book a demo' (quicklyster.ca, _blank) + 'Sign in or Register' button. Hero orbs (3 × .orb), ::after display:none, ::before animation retops-bg-drift live. Hero + footer CTAs testids all match spec. Header and footer logos both h-36 (144px). /auth renders with mode toggle, form fields, Google btn, book-demo link. Full e2e: register with fresh creds → /dashboard, logout → re-login with same creds → /dashboard. Executive view has 12 .kpi-num elements all Instrument Serif + tabular-nums; zero legacy 'font-display text-3xl num-hero' elements remain. No 'Sign in with Google' text on landing.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers behind K8s ingress. `identifier = f"{ip}:{email}"` uses request.client.host, but 6 consecutive failed logins showed up in db.login_attempts under 2 different IPs (10.79.131.66 and 10.79.131.71) → each counter capped at 2-4, never hit 5, so the endpoint keeps returning 401 instead of 429. Fix: parse X-Forwarded-For (or use only the email as identifier) so rate-limit keys are stable across proxy hops.

ui_bugs.issue: Value renders as '+-1.3%' — the '+' prefix is being prepended unconditionally even when the delta is already negative. Likely `{prefix}{value}` in ExecutiveView.jsx should check sign before adding '+'.

rca of the issue: BRUTE FORCE 429 FAILURE RCA — Reproduction: send 6 consecutive POST /api/auth/login with same email but wrong password. Expected: 6th returns 429. Observed: 6th returns 401. Root cause: in _check_brute_force/_record_failed_login the `identifier` key is composed from `request.client.host` (the immediate TCP peer, i.e., the K8s ingress pod) + email. Dumping db.login_attempts after the test shows two rows with identical email but different IPs (10.79.131.66 count=4, 10.79.131.71 count=2) — neither ever hits the count>=5 threshold because requests round-robin across proxy pods. Mitigation: (a) parse request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip() as the true client IP before composing the identifier, OR (b) drop IP entirely and key on email only (simpler, still effective since email is unique). Either fix should make the existing test pass without further changes.
